David —

We started seeing a sudden jump in 5xxs and timeouts for inference calls from our production fleet around 07:55 PDT. Error rate jumped to ~18% and median tail latency spiked from ~180ms to >1200ms. The attached PNG has the request-rate and 5xx overlays; the svc logs (snippet) show connection resets and repeated failed handshakes to your AZ endpoint az-eastbay-1.

We have thousands of active users hitting Sarapharm’s medication reconciliation flow; this is impacting critical workflows. Can you confirm whether this is an issue on Redwood’s side or something between our network? We need an explicit plan for traffic steering to another region and expected timeline.

–Samuel
Senior Platform Engineer
SaraPharm

Quick update from SRE triage:
- Telemetry indicates a control-plane route re-propagation event around 07:50 that coincides with the spike. Serving nodes are healthy in the fabric but we’re seeing a mismatch between the front-door routing table and backend gateway availability — likely a partial gateway network flap in az-eastbay-1.
- Network team reports intermittent packet loss on two border switches affecting our LB tiers; mitigations in flight.

Recommended mitigation: short-term geo-fallback for SaraPharm routing to avoid client-side retries hitting the degraded AZ. Two options:
A) Canary 10% to az-westcoast-2 for 15 mins, monitor 5xx & latency; if green, 100% cut-over.
B) Immediate 100% cut-over to az-westcoast-2 for 60 mins while we stabilize az-eastbay-1.

I recommend option A for a safer rollout given SaraPharm’s production criticality. Marcus — can you confirm capacity and any per-account throttles we need to adjust? I’ll stand by to toggle routing rules and open a temporary cache pre-warm policy for SaraPharm to reduce cold-KV penalty.

Hannah
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

Capacity check: az-westcoast-2 has available headroom to accept SaraPharm traffic at current qps. No per-account rate-limiters will be hit if we ramp gradually to 100% within 10 minutes. A few operational notes:
- We need to patch the per-route sticky session TTL to 30s to reduce inference cache misses during the cut. I can apply that immediately.
- If we do a 10% canary, pre-warm of hot KV prefixes will trim p95 latency by ~40ms. I’ll trigger a targeted pre-warm job once routing rules are updated.
- Routing change is a config flip in our edge control plane and will take ~60s to propagate globally; plan accordingly.

I support option A (10% canary -> ramp) unless the customer requests immediate switch.

Marcus

Samuel — thanks for reporting and for the logs. Proposed customer comms below; please confirm whether we should proceed with a canary or immediate full cut-over. We’ll only act after your sign-off.

Customer message (draft):
Hi Samuel / Ops team —

We’re seeing increased 5xx and timeouts originating from our EastBay availability zone (az-eastbay-1). Our SRE team has identified a partial network flap impacting the edge gateway in that AZ. To restore reliable service quickly, we propose to shift traffic to our secondary region (az-westcoast-2) using a staged approach:

- Step 1 (canary): 10% of production traffic redirected to az-westcoast-2 for 15 minutes; monitor error and latency metrics.
- Step 2 (ramp): If canary looks healthy, we’ll progressively increase to 100% over ~10 minutes.
- Step 3 (stabilize): Keep traffic on westcoast-2 while we validate and fully remediate eastbay gateways; we’ll provide an ETA for return to primary AZ.

Expected impact: transient additional tail latency for warmed-up flows (~20-80ms) during the first minute; otherwise service should remain available. No planned data loss; session stickiness retained via TTL update.

Please reply ASAP with your preference: CANARY or IMMEDIATE. If we don’t hear back in 10 minutes, we will start the 10% canary to reduce customer impact.

—Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
